Event-Wise Numeric Exponential Kernel Calculations

exp_kernel_step.Rd

Advance kernel components, apply an optional event update, or invert supplied integrated-driver targets. These experimental deterministic interfaces generate no random numbers and do not run a simulation loop.

Usage

exp_kernel_step(kernel, component, dt, type = NULL, mark = 1,
                integrate = TRUE)
exp_kernel_wait(kernel, component, mu, residual)

Arguments

kernel

An exp_kernel_spec or convertible numeric hspec. Decay rates must be equal within each row.

component

Finite current kernel components, excluding baseline. A scalar expands to all components; a matrix matches the kernel shape, and a vector of matching length uses R's column-major order.

dt

A finite nonnegative scalar interval.

type

An event-type row index whose mapped columns are updated, or NULL to advance without applying an event.

mark

A finite scalar event mark. The default is one.

integrate

Logical; also return the component-wise interval integrals?

mu

Finite nonnegative baseline, scalar or one value per event type.

residual

Nonnegative integrated-driver targets, one per event type. Positive infinity is allowed. Targets are supplied by the calling model.

Details

The specification contains no evolving state. Step returns the pre-event components after decay and the post-event components after mapped alpha addition followed by eta times (mark minus one). Signed components are not clipped. Baseline contributions are excluded from step integrals. A zero interval still updates when type is supplied.

Wait inverts, independently for each row i, $$A_i(t) = \mu_i t + C_i (1-\exp(-\beta_i t))/\beta_i,$$ where C is the row sum of the current components. Kernel row sums must be nonnegative and decreasing; the existing simulation cancellation guard is retained for signed components. A zero target yields zero. With zero baseline, a target at or above the finite total integral yields infinity. No event is selected and no residual distribution is evaluated by this function. Summation and root-solving order match the existing equal-rate FRPP arrival calculation; component integrals are not separately summed during inversion.

The caller owns residual generation, event selection, initial-state policy, counts, output recording and callback behavior. A simulator must check its current state before drawing new residuals and must not restart another backend after consuming draws. These functions do not change the existing Hawkes or legacy FRPP paths, or the meaning of emhawkes.engine.

Value

Step returns a list of before and after component matrices, and integral when requested. Wait returns a numeric candidate waiting-time vector in event-type row order. Inputs are not modified.

See also

exp_kernel_spec, exp_kernel_replay

Examples

kernel <- exp_kernel_spec(.2, 1)
wait <- exp_kernel_wait(kernel, component = .1, mu = .3, residual = .7)
exp_kernel_step(kernel, component = .1, dt = wait, type = 1)
#> $before
#>            [,1]
#> [1,] 0.01296127
#> 
#> $after
#>           [,1]
#> [1,] 0.2129613
#> 
#> $integral
#>            [,1]
#> [1,] 0.08703873
#>
